patterns.title: Circular Prerequisites and Bootstrapping

sources.title: Python Software Foundation, graphlib — Functionality to operate with graph-like structures
sources.supports: A complete topological ordering exists exactly for a directed acyclic graph; cycle detection can still permit independent ready work.
sources.boundary: Formal result for a correctly specified finite prerequisite graph; not evidence that a real institutional requirement is necessary or immutable.

sources.title: Bootstrappable Builds, Best Practices
sources.supports: Alternative language implementations, minimal compiler implementations, simpler build-system routes, and provenance of bootstrap binaries.
sources.boundary: Specialist engineering recommendations. No cross-domain effectiveness rate or guarantee is inferred.

sources.title: Rust Compiler Development Guide, What Bootstrapping Does
sources.supports: A precompiled stage-zero compiler and standard library produce a compiler from current source, followed by later build stages.
sources.boundary: Primary current process documentation, checked on 31 October 2026. No exact release compatibility claim, build command, benchmark, or security guarantee is made.

sources.title: Bootstrappable Builds
sources.supports: The compiler chicken-and-egg problem and motivation to examine the initial binary seed and its production chain.
sources.boundary: Project goals and explanation; successful bootstrapping alone does not prove source-to-binary correspondence or eliminate all trust assumptions.

sources.title: NIST Computer Security Resource Center, bootstrapping
sources.supports: Network-layer onboarding introduces sufficient initial information for trust and a secure channel, potentially through a human-assisted out-of-band process.
sources.boundary: Glossary definition sourced to NIST IR 8350; not a general recommendation to bypass authentication or evidence of outcomes.

sources.title: AAA, Fourteen Reasons Why Your Car Will Not Start
sources.supports: Explains starter operation and charging by an alternator while the engine runs. Supports distinguishing discharged battery, starter, and charging-system faults.
sources.boundary: Specialist practical explanation of physical dependencies; not proof that external starting repairs a fault, restores full charge, or applies identically to all powertrains. Article provides no equipment-connection instructions.
sources.read_method: Opened and read starting-battery, alternator, and starter sections.

patterns.short_description: Identify a chain of prerequisites that has no available first step, then supply a usable starting condition or authorize a different entry route.
use_when: What supplies energy before the engine can recharge its battery?
goals: Recognize the concrete predicament before terminology.
Preserve defining assumptions and distinctions without calculations.
Evaluate intervention authority, costs, residual risks, and changed assumptions.
mechanisms: Supply a compatible starting source available before ordinary operation.
Assumes discharge only. Assistance costs resources; faults and the cause of discharge still need attention.

example_structure.scenario: Conventional engine-driven charging system, discharged but serviceable starting battery, otherwise functioning starter and charging system. External energy supplies the initial condition; a start does not prove full charge or repair. Dependency-state analogy distinguished from a topological-order theorem.
example_structure.changed_relationship: Supply a compatible starting source available before ordinary operation.
example_structure.residual_constraints: Assumes discharge only. Assistance costs resources; faults and the cause of discharge still need attention.
example_structure.evidence: Hypothetical scenario and stipulated continuation; no expected result presented as measured outcome. Qualitative ranking and ordering replace illustrative arithmetic.

visual.question: What supplies energy before the engine can recharge its battery?
visual.alternative_text: Hypothetical qualitative illustration. Battery charge enables the starter and engine; the running engine enables later alternator charging. Change: Supply a compatible starting source available before ordinary operation. Limitation: Assumes discharge only. Assistance costs resources; faults and the cause of discharge still need attention.
visual.caption: Hypothetical illustration. The upper cycle distinguishes initial stored energy from later replenishment. The lower route supplies a seed without changing the car’s normal starting requirement. A successful start does not diagnose the battery or charging system, or establish full recharge.
